req.title: Delete unknown returns 404
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 when DELETE targets a non-existent task id.

doc.reasoning: R-TASK-014 requires DELETE /tasks/{task_id} to return HTTP 404 when the task_id does not exist. Three test cases are designed: (1) a positive case confirming a known-existing task (id=1) is deleted with 204, verifying the happy path and that the delete endpoint works at all; (2) a negative case sending a clearly non-existent id (id=99999) and asserting exactly 404 with the correct detail message, catching status-code mutations and string-constant mutations; (3) a boundary case using id=21 (one beyond the highest seeded id=20) to catch off-by-one mutations in any existence check, and also verifying id=20 returns 204 to confirm the boundary is tight. Each test uses an in-memory SQLite override via dependency injection so the pre-loaded fixture rows are present and tests are fully isolated.

tests.name: test_delete_existing_task_returns_204
preconditions: Task with id=1 exists in the pre-loaded dataset
Database is initialised with all 20 seed rows
trace: R-TASK-014 — confirms the success path so mutations that always return 404 are killed
tests.executable:
import os, tempfile
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
from app.main import app
from app.database import get_db
from app import models

tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
DB_URL = f"sqlite:///{tmp}/test_pos.db"
engine = create_engine(DB_URL, connect_args={"check_same_thread": False})
TestingSession = sessionmaker(autocommit=False, autoflush=False, bind=engine)
models.Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)

db = TestingSession()
db.add(models.Task(id=1, title="Read chapter 5", description="desc", completed=True))
db.commit()
db.close()

def override_get_db():
    db = TestingSession()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()

app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = override_get_db
client = TestClient(app)

def test_delete_existing_task_returns_204():
    r = client.delete("/tasks/1")
    assert r.status_code == 204
    assert r.content == b""

test_delete_existing_task_returns_204()
app.dependency_overrides.clear()

tests.name: test_delete_boundary_ids_around_max_seeded
preconditions: Task with id=20 exists (highest seeded id)
No task with id=21 exists (one beyond the highest seeded id)
expected: DELETE /tasks/21 returns HTTP 404 with detail 'Task with id 21 not found'
Second DELETE /tasks/20 returns HTTP 404 with detail 'Task with id 20 not found'
trace: R-TASK-014 — BVA at max seeded id boundary; catches off-by-one mutations in existence checks and state-transition from exists to deleted
tests.executable:
import os, tempfile
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
from app.main import app
from app.database import get_db
from app import models

tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
DB_URL = f"sqlite:///{tmp}/test_bva.db"
engine = create_engine(DB_URL, connect_args={"check_same_thread": False})
TestingSession = sessionmaker(autocommit=False, autoflush=False, bind=engine)
models.Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)

db = TestingSession()
db.add(models.Task(id=20, title="Reply to emails", description="desc", completed=False))
db.commit()
db.close()

def override_get_db():
    db = TestingSession()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()

app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = override_get_db
client = TestClient(app)

def test_delete_boundary_ids_around_max_seeded():
    r21 = client.delete("/tasks/21")
    assert r21.status_code == 404
    assert r21.json()["detail"] == "Task with id 21 not found"
    r20 = client.delete("/tasks/20")
    assert r20.status_code == 204
    assert r20.content == b""
    r20_again = client.delete("/tasks/20")
    assert r20_again.status_code == 404
    assert r20_again.json()["detail"] == "Task with id 20 not found"

test_delete_boundary_ids_around_max_seeded()
app.dependency_overrides.clear()
